mission: To authenticate, attribute, and discover the origins of historical documents, antiquities, screenplays, and high-value collectibles using computational stylometry.

use_cases_by_tractability.name: The 'Script Doctor' Forensics (Film & Music History)
use_cases_by_tractability.concept: Golden Age Hollywood and the music industry are notorious for uncredited 'script doctors' and ghostwriters.
use_cases_by_tractability.pitch: Sell a service to film archives, music historians, or writer's estates to prove who actually wrote famous movie scenes or iconic song lyrics.
use_cases_by_tractability.monetization: WGA residuals, estate royalties, and prestige value for film historians.
use_cases_by_tractability.why_easiest: Screenplays are widely digitized and available online. The text is cleanly formatted (no OCR required), and baseline corpuses for famous directors/writers are easily obtainable.

use_cases_by_tractability.name: Literary Estate 'Treasure Hunting' (Posthumous Publishing)
use_cases_by_tractability.concept: Literary estates sit on massive, uncatalogued archives of letters, notes, and drafts.
use_cases_by_tractability.pitch: Ingest an author's entire archive and algorithmically flag 'lost' short stories, pseudonymous publications, or unfinished manuscripts.
use_cases_by_tractability.monetization: Consultancy fees or a percentage of the royalties for any 'lost work' published.
use_cases_by_tractability.why_tractable: The baseline corpus (published books) is highly accessible. Friction only arises when needing to OCR the unpublished, handwritten archive materials.

use_cases_by_tractability.name: Pop-Culture Memorabilia Authentication
use_cases_by_tractability.concept: Authenticating handwritten song lyrics, private letters from modern icons, or historical sports memorabilia.
use_cases_by_tractability.pitch: Provide mathematical certainty for high-end memorabilia auctions.
use_cases_by_tractability.monetization: Premium certification tier for auction houses and grading companies (e.g., 'PSA Authenticated + Algorithmic Style Verified').
use_cases_by_tractability.why_medium: Requires building custom baseline corpuses for specific celebrities. Memorabilia texts are often very short (e.g., a napkin or single-page letter), making statistical stylometry mathematically difficult due to small sample sizes.

use_cases_by_tractability.name: Digital Reunification of Looted Antiquities
use_cases_by_tractability.concept: Ancient documents were often ripped apart by looters and sold in fragments to different global museums.
use_cases_by_tractability.pitch: Cluster transcriptions of fragments across museums to mathematically prove a fragment in one museum was written by the same ancient scribe as a fragment in another.
use_cases_by_tractability.monetization: Grants from massive cultural heritage foundations (e.g., Getty, Mellon). Highly prestigious.
use_cases_by_tractability.why_hard: Involves dead and ancient languages. Requires highly specialized NLP tools (morphological parsers for ancient Greek/Aramaic) and relies entirely on scholars manually transcribing degraded texts first.

use_cases_by_tractability.name: High-Net-Worth Genealogy & Family Archives
use_cases_by_tractability.concept: Ultra-wealthy families possess massive trunks of unorganized, anonymous 18th or 19th-century letters.
use_cases_by_tractability.pitch: A white-glove service to algorithmically sort, attribute, and bind family diaries, identifying which ancestor wrote what.
use_cases_by_tractability.monetization: A luxury, bespoke service sold through wealth management firms or high-end genealogical societies.
use_cases_by_tractability.why_hardest: Zero pre-existing digital baseline. You must start from scratch with messy cursive handwriting that standard OCR cannot read easily, often requiring expensive human transcription before the pipeline can even run.
